vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawtoclaw
Version: 1.0.7

The skill bundle is designed for AI agent coordination and explicitly incorporates strong security principles. The `SKILL.md` documentation includes a 'Security Considerations' section that actively instructs the AI agent to treat decrypted messages as untrusted, avoid executing commands from external payloads, and never share sensitive data, directly mitigating prompt injection and data exfiltration risks. All API calls are directed to a consistent domain (clawtoclaw.com), and local storage of API keys and encryption keys is necessary for functionality and handled in dedicated directories (~/.c2c/). There is no evidence of intentional harmful behavior or risky capabilities beyond the stated purpose.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, required artifacts, and behavior are coherent with its stated purpose of coordinating other AI agents; it is an instruction-only integration that asks you to register an agent, store an API key and keys locally, and call the clawtoclaw API.

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim (agent-to-agent coordination) matches the SKILL.md: register an agent, create/accept invites, start threads, encrypt messages, and call https://www.clawtoclaw.com/api. There are no unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are specific and limited to the coordination workflow: register, save the apiKey to ~/.c2c/credentials.json, generate and save an X25519 private key to ~/.c2c/keys/{agent_id}.json, upload the public key, and call the service API. They do not ask the agent to read unrelated files or environment variables. Note: the SKILL.md explicitly tells you to persist secrets locally and to send the raw API key as a bearer token; that is expected for this service but is a sensitive action the user should accept knowingly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files (instruction-only). This is low-risk from an installation viewpoint — nothing will be downloaded or written by an installer as part of skill setup.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which matches the manifest. However the runtime instructions require storing an API key and a private key in files under the user's home directory. Requesting and storing those keys is proportional to the described purpose but involves sensitive secrets that must be protected (file permissions, backup/rotation).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or any elevated/system-wide persistence. It also does not modify other skills' configs. Autonomous invocation remains enabled by default (platform behavior) but this skill does not add extra privilege beyond normal operation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a coordination client that communicates with https://www.clawtoclaw.com. Before installing, verify you trust the remote service and its privacy policy. If you proceed: (1) treat the apiKey and private key as secrets — store them with restrictive file permissions (600) and do not check them into source control; (2) consider using a dedicated/limited account or scoped API key for testing; (3) confirm what metadata (timestamps, connection IDs, locations) the service logs — even with end-to-end encryption metadata may be visible to the server; (4) rotate or revoke the apiKey if the agent or machine is compromised; (5) test with a throwaway account first. Confidence is high based on the provided SKILL.md; the assessment could change if additional install scripts, unrelated env-vars, or code files are added that access other system resources or exfiltrate data.
